title: Autonomic cost fallback playbook and costctl dry-run evaluator
author: Marco Alvarez
description:
Context: We frequently tune batching, cache and quantization defaults to reduce per-token costs, but changes that improve unit economics can sometimes surface subtle quality regressions or unexpected latency spikes for small tenant segments. This PR introduces an end-to-end operational playbook plus a lightweight CLI evaluator (costctl) to safely propose cost optimizations and perform staged, observable rollouts with automatic rollback triggers.

What this PR adds (high level):
- costctl evaluate --dry-run: simulates the application of a set of candidate changes (batch size, cache TTLs, quant profiles) against historical traces and returns estimated unit-econ deltas and risk signals (quality-regression score, tail-latency delta, token-saved estimate). The evaluator runs a fast deterministic simulation using the existing replay harness (sampling-based) and a new lightweight scoring function that flags risky changes.
- Playbook primitives: a JSON/YAML playbook format (playbooks/cost-fallback-v1.yaml) that encodes staged rollout steps: shadow-canary -> 5% canary -> 25% ramp -> full rollout, with configurable rollback signals and observed-metrics thresholds.
- Canary shadowing mode in serving runtime: a non-intrusive shadow path that computes responses from the candidate model/config but does not affect caller latency; it reports divergence traces and a compact regression fingerprint to telemetry for post-hoc analysis.
- Auto-rollback engine: a controller that monitors chosen SLOs (quality regressions, p99 latency, error-rate) and automatically reverts an in-flight rollout if thresholds are crossed. The engine supports automatic mitigation options: throttle back to previous batch/cache settings, revert quant profile, or pause rollout.
- Observability surface: dashboards and telemetry tags to show simulated vs observed unit-econ, divergence counts, regression fingerprints, and rollout state transitions. Also emits compact audit events for compliance.

Why this is different: previous PRs focused on generating recommended defaults. This work is operational: it safely closes the loop—simulate, stage, observe, and rollback—so teams can evaluate and apply cost improvements with bounded risk. The emphasis is on predictable, automated rollback behavior and an auditable evaluation path.

Implementation notes:
- costctl was added as a small Go binary (cmd/costctl) that orchestrates trace replay (using replay/sampler) and hits the new evaluator service (pkg/evaluator). The binary supports --dry-run and --apply (apply currently requires feature flag and elevated RBAC).
- The evaluator uses a deterministic sampling policy and a new scoring heuristic (pkg/evaluator/score.go) that combines: estimated token-savings, model-response divergence fingerprint (hash of structured fields), and synthetic latency delta computed from per-token kernel predictions. The heuristic weights are tunable via feature flags.
- The runtime changes include a shadowing hook (runtime/shadow.go) and a lightweight divergence recorder (telemetry/divergence_v1.proto) that attaches fingerprints without recording full responses.
- Playbook definitions live under playbooks/ and are validated during CI.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for evaluator scoring (pkg/evaluator/score_test.go) and playbook validation.
- Integration tests: simulator integration test that runs costctl evaluate --dry-run on archived traces (ci/traces/sample-2026-01.json.gz) and asserts estimates are consistent within a tolerance.
- Staging rollout: deployed to staging cluster for 48h with synthetic traffic; we ran three simulated canary rollouts and verified auto-rollback triggers on an injected regression (added in integration test harness).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag gated in main.
2) Enable costctl evaluate --dry-run for platform/infra users.
3) After 2 weeks of observational use and no false positives, enable apply for limited SRE users.
4) Gradual enable for product teams; monitor metrics and cadence.

Risks and mitigations:
- False negatives: simulator might miss rare divergence patterns. Mitigation: conservative defaults for rollout thresholds; require at least one human review for high-risk changes.
- Telemetry volume: divergence fingerprints are compact (single 64-bit hash + counters) and emitted at low sampling rate by default.
- Security: apply path requires RBAC and audit logging.

Files changed summary: modified runtime to add shadow hooks; added costctl; playbooks and tests; dashboards and migration for telemetry fields.

Related work: ENG-2001 (cost-sandboxing), ENG-2042 (batching defaults CI harness).

Notes for reviewers: please pay attention to the divergence fingerprint format and the default thresholds in playbooks/cost-fallback-v1.yaml. I intentionally chose conservative defaults to reduce blast radius for initial deployment.

feat: add evaluator service and scoring heuristic (pkg/evaluator) with unit tests
feat: runtime shadow hook and divergence recorder (runtime/shadow.go, telemetry)
chore: playbook definitions and validation, dashboards and docs
test: integration harness for ci using archived traces and injected regressions
release_notes: Introduces costctl dry-run evaluator, staged rollout playbook primitives and an auto-rollback controller to safely apply batching/cache/quant changes. Feature gated and initially conservative; see docs/operational/cost_playbook.md for usage.
review_comments: Lena Ortiz: Nice end-to-end. Two nits: 1) Can we make the fingerprint algorithm explicit (xxhash64?) and 2) add a config toggle for sampling rate in telemetry?
Author (Marco): Reply: switched to xxhash64 and exposed sampling_rate flag in telemetry config. Updated tests accordingly.

Hiro Tanaka: The auto-rollback thresholds seem aggressive for p99 on multi-tenant noisy services. Suggest bumping the p99 delta threshold and require two consecutive evaluation windows before rollback.
Author (Marco): Agree, implemented hysteresis (two windows) and bumped defaults. Added an env var to tune behavior per-cluster.
Priya Desai: Integration tests are solid. One request: document RBAC for apply path in README.costctl.md.
Author (Marco): Added RBAC section to README.costctl.md and auth/rbac_rules.yml.
